operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order waives, for one named employee, the limit in section 1 of EO 9721 on the period treated as leave of absence and deems him on leave from March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957 for the purposes of EO 9721, as amended. research_rationale:
EO 11303 (1966-09-12, 31 FR 11963) modifies EO 9721, as amended by EO 10103, by waiving for Reginald C. Price the limitation in section 1 on the period during which an employee is considered on leave of absence, and deeming him on leave from March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957 for the purpose of all rights and benefits under EO 9721, as amended. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11303.txt, 31 FR 11963, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed its number, title and date against the census register (signature line OCR "September 1% , 1966"; filing line "Filed, Sept. 12,1966"). The order is a single paragraph with one operative command, so the dossier's single clause is the complete inventory. EO 10804 (signed 1959-02-12; held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10804.txt, 24 FR 1147, and held American Presidency Project text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-10804-delegating-the-civil-service-commission-the-authority-the-president.txt, sha256 41b6c5dd182ed7ccad05cc344eca506899f5c377f74aae393d04bc880af51215) revoked EO 9721 and EO 10103 seven years before this order was signed. Its section 2 lists "Executive Order No. 9721 ' of May 10, 1946; Executive Order No. 10103 of February 1, 1950; and Executive Order No. 10774 of July 25, 1958, insofar as it affects any employee covered by section 6 (a) of the International Atomic Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957" (APP text). The limiting phrase uses the singular "it" and follows only the EO 10774 item, so I read it as limiting EO 10774 alone; EO 9721 and EO 10103 were revoked generally, subject to the section's two exceptions: each order "shall be considered to remain in effect with respect to any employee subject thereto serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who does not elect to have coverage under the latter Act", and remains in effect "for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested under each such order prior to the date of the enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act" (APP text). So when EO 11303 was signed on 1966-09-12, EO 9721 as amended by EO 10103 survived only within those exceptions. EO 10804 cannot be this order's end: it precedes the order, and no held source shows that it extinguished a command issued afterwards. EO 11303 rests on its own cited authority (the Civil Service Act and section 1753 of the Revised Statutes) and credits a leave period, March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957, that ended before the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act (cited in EO 10804 at 72 Stat. 961, the 1958 volume; the held texts do not give the exact enactment date). The held texts do not say whether the 1966 waiver was treated as falling within the saving for rights and benefits vested before that Act or as a fresh grant; under either reading the order operated from its signing until EO 12553 revoked it by number, so the question does not move the end date. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes EO 11303 by number (table row "11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations"); the same table lists 9721 and the row "10103 Amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations", so EO 12553 also revoked whatever remained of the parent order and its amendment on the same day. The first end of EO 11303 is that express revocation. The waiver is a one-person act that took effect on the order's date; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 the exhausted waiver is distinguished from the surviving consequence (the credited leave period and the rights that rest on it), and no held source shows an earlier cessation of the command. The alternative reading, that the self-executing deeming was exhausted when the order took effect on 1966-09-12, is disclosed for the reviewer; I did not adopt it because the deeming operates for the purpose "of all rights and benefits provided by Executive Order No. 9721", as amended, and EO 9721 remained in effect for vested rights and benefits under EO 10804's saving until EO 12553 revoked it. Price', which found only this order's own texts and copies of EO 12553; a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters). Separately, I read the held FR and APP texts of EO 10804 in full because it revoked the parent order in 1959; it does not name EO 11303, which was issued later.
